Subject: Service coverage & remedy framework - Brightfield AI

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is enthusiastic about Redwood's throughput. Procurement asked me to kick off an SLA conversation so we can align the standard uptime targets and how monthly service credits would be calculated. A few asks from our side to frame the discussion: 

- Given our batched inference patterns (heavy morning peaks) and cross-region traffic, would Redwood consider a baseline uptime of 99.7% rather than 99.95 in return for a simpler credit formula?
- We also need an API latency commitment (p95) for our real-time routes — currently targeting 350ms p95 for the US region.
- How do you handle maintenance windows by region and emergency maintenance carve-outs?
- For credits, we'd like a predictable monthly calculation (e.g., % of monthly bill × multiplier) rather than ad-hoc credits.

Can you share a suggested draft and any alternative structures you typically offer? We want to move quickly — procurement is aiming to wrap commercial terms in the coming two weeks.

Thanks,
Sara Kline
Head of Ops, Brightfield AI

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@brightfield.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service coverage & remedy framework - Brightfield AI

Sara — thanks for the clear framing. Pushing back a bit on the baseline: our production customers rely on a 99.95% availability baseline to justify standard multi-tenant routing and shared capacity economics. Dropping to 99.7% materially increases risk and isolation needs.

Proposal (high level):
- Availability baseline: 99.95% across US (can offer 99.9% for EU with regional pilot).
- Tiered monthly service credit bands:
  • 99.95% - 99.90% => 10% of monthly service fee
  • 99.90% - 99.50% => 25% of monthly service fee
  • <99.50% => 50% of monthly service fee (subject to cap)
- Monthly credit cap: limited to 30% of monthly invoice (we can negotiate upward with dedicated pools).
- Latency: we can commit to p95 <= 350ms for our "interactive" plan when routed to regional capacity. For batched inference routes, latency SLAs are looser — suggest an objective (not credit-bearing) threshold of p95 <= 600ms.
- Maintenance: standard scheduled maintenance windows up to 6 hours/month per region with 72h notice; emergency maintenance carve-out up to 4 hours with post-event report.

Attached is a draft SLA that reflects the above plus metric definitions and a sample credit calc. If you need a lower availability baseline we can structure it as a short-term ramp with a dedicated capacity add-on (pilot).

I'll loop in Laura for legal redlines and Ben for commercial trade-offs.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Service coverage & remedy framework - Brightfield AI

Jonas — quick legal check. A couple of redlines and clarifications I'd like to insert before we send to Brightfield as a formal draft: 

1) "Service credits" only — explicit language that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy (no direct refunds or offsets against committed spend) and that credits apply to subscription fees not third-party pass-throughs.
2) Exclusions — customer-caused issues (misconfigured routing, client-side SDK errors, DDoS initiated by client's customers) must be carved out. We should include a short list of obvious exclusions and a tie-in to a diagnostic runbook.
3) Measurement window — compute availability on a monthly rolling window using platform telemetry; include link to the metrics spec (we'll reference the Drive doc).
4) Maintenance — cap scheduled maintenance to 8 hours/month if we need more, it will trigger a separate notice and not count toward credits. Keep 48 hours' notice minimum for scheduled maintenance.
5) Force majeure and third-party cloud provider outages — call these out explicitly so credits are not owed for provider-wide outages outside our control.

I'll prepare suggested wording and insert placeholders for the credit calculation formula. Please confirm we keep the 30% monthly cap for now; if Brightfield wants a higher cap we should only offer that with a committed spend/discount trade.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Commercial: credit cap trade and pilot offer (BF-2027-043)

Sara — quick commercial note to accelerate alignment:

If Brightfield is willing to accept the 99.95% baseline with the tiered credit bands and a 30% monthly cap, we can offer the following commercial concessions: 
- 10% committed usage discount for the first 12 months (applies to hosted API spend).
- 3-month dedicated-capacity pilot (discounted by 25% for pilot months) to shore up peak reliability for your morning batch workloads.
- A 45-day instrumentation phase to validate latency measurements and routing behavior before the SLA goes live.

We can include these as a separate SOW / commercial schedule. Deal ID BF-2027-043. Pricing sheet attached for optics.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with procurement to finalize.

Thanks Jonas/Ben/Laura — helpful clarity and quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from procurement and ops: 

- Brightfield prefers a slightly more generous monthly cap on credits given our risk tolerance during ramp — can you consider a 50% monthly cap for the first 6 months of production (after which it reverts to 30%)? We see this as a temporary protection while we stabilize traffic patterns.
- Latency SLA: we need p95 <= 350ms to be credit-bearing for the API layer (not only the interactive plan). If dedicated pilot is required to meet that, we understand — but we want the metric in the SLA and an associated timeline to achieve it.
- Emergency maintenance carve-out: ops requests that emergencies under 4 hours not trigger credits provided a remediation post-mortem is delivered within 48 hours. That's aligned with your note but please confirm in drafting.

If you can accept the 6-month 50% monthly cap ramp and include the API p95 commitment with an agreed instrumentation phase, procurement is prepared to move the Redlines review to signature within 10 business days.

Best,
Sara
Sara Kline | Head of Ops, Brightfield AI
